jobs.title: Director - Geological Data & Database Management
jobs.description:
Start Date: ASAP

Work Model: Hybrid

Location: Downtown Toronto

(outside Union Station – TTC & GO accessible)

Dress Code: Business Casual A Great Place to Work

Who We Are

Founded in 1993, Kinross is a Canadian-based senior gold mining company with operations and projects in the United States, Brazil, Mauritania, Chile and Canada. Our focus on delivering value is based on our four core values of Putting People First, Outstanding Corporate Citizenship, High Performance Culture, and Rigorous Financial Discipline.

Mining responsibly is a priority for Kinross, and we foster a culture that makes responsible mining and operational success inseparable. Our values-based approach ensures that sustainability and our environmental, social and governance commitments are a core part of our strategy and plans for future growth. In line with our values, we also aim to build meaningful partnerships with all of our stakeholders, including communities, shareholders, employees, governments and suppliers.

Kinross maintains listings on the Toronto Stock Exchange (symbol: K) and the New York Stock Exchange (symbol: KGC).

Job Summary

The Director, Geological Data & Database Management is a senior technical leadership role accountable for designing, implementing, and governing a company-wide database management system across all exploration, project, and operating sites. This is a hands-on leadership position: the Director is responsible for maintaining and updating company standards and ensuring sites adopt/adhere to them, ensuring standardization of database software and structures across all sites, and building and managing a team of database administrators and analysts.

Key Responsibilities

Ensure standardization of the company geologic database platform across all exploration, project, and operating sites, including migration of legacy and existing site databases where required.
Maintain database standards for structure, content, and required tables at each project maturity point (Setup, Initial Drilling, Infill, Scoping, PFS, FS, and Operations), and ensure sites are equipped to meet them.
Lead selection, configuration, and lifecycle management of database software and related tools, in partnership with IT.
Ensure QA/QC protocols are implemented and auditable per internal standards.
Establish and audit data security controls across all sites: layered/restricted access by user type, edit tracking and audit trails, and automatic, regular backups including offsite storage.
Define and enforce the separation between dynamic project databases and frozen, dated resource-model databases used for reserve/resource work.
Lead systematic, scheduled reviews of database quality across all sites and drive corrective action plans ahead of each project maturity point.
Initiate and lead internal and external audits as required.
Build, lead, and develop the company database management function, including hiring and mentoring site and project database administrators and analysts.
liase with exploration management, KTS, and site geology teams to ensure database structures support geological, resource, and reserve modelling requirements.
Develop and deliver training and documented procedures for database administrators, geologists, and technical staff on data entry standards, QA/QC execution, and system use.
Maintain and continuously improve governing documentation (standards guides, database structure references.)
Report on database health, compliance, and risk to senior technical and executive leadership.

Qualifications And Skills

Education and Experience

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Geology, Earth Sciences, Geological Engineering, or a related field.
10+ years of progressive experience in mineral exploration or mining geology, including significant experience in geological database design, administration, or data management.
5+ years in a senior or leadership role managing database systems, technical teams, or data governance programs across multiple sites or projects.
Demonstrated experience implementing or administering industry-standard geological database platforms (e.g., acQuire, Fusion, Datashed, or comparable systems) at a multi-site scale.

Technical & Leadership Skills

Deep understanding of relational database structures as applied to drill hole data (collar, survey, lithology, assay, QA/QC, geotechnical, geometallurgical, density, and related tables).
Strong knowledge of QA/QC protocols, chain-of-custody procedures, and data security/access-control best practices in a geological or mining context.
Proven ability to lead large-scale systems and change management initiatives across geographically distributed sites.
Excellent people-leadership skills, with experience building and managing teams, including remote or site-based staff and dotted-line reporting relationships.
Strong communication skills, able to translate technical database requirements for both site-level technical staff and executive leadership.
Willingness and ability to travel regularly to exploration, project, and operating sites, including remote locations.

Compensation and Total Rewards

The base salary range for this role is $180,000 to $220,000 CAD plus a target Short-Term Incentive bonus of 30%, 30% (LTI) and group benefit coverage. The hiring range reflects our targeted compensation framework for the role. The actual offer will be determined through a comprehensive evaluation of each candidate’s experience, capabilities, and potential impact, along with consideration of internal equity, team structure, and benchmark market data for similar positions. In addition to base salary, Kinross offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support employee well-being, performance, and long-term development.

Use of AI in Our Hiring Process

We use AI-enabled tools to help sort and review applications based on job-related criteria. All hiring decisions, including who moves forward in the process, are made by a human.

Existing Vacancy

This job posting is for an existing vacancy.

jobs.title: Artificial Intelligence Strategy Practice Leader
jobs.description:
Required

As Artificial Intelligence Strategy Practice Leader, you play a key role in the Office of the Chief Data and Analytics Officer, which helps various sectors across the organization generate, prioritize and implement analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) initiatives. You help teams take full advantage of data and AI to achieve their business objectives. To do this, you work closely with business partners to understand their challenges, identify opportunities and align analytical efforts with the organization’s strategic priorities. You also conduct strategic monitoring of AI developments and market practices. Working with the sectors, you lead efforts to find opportunities based on business processes and take part in discussions on transforming them through AI. By doing so, you help the organization identify tasks that need improvement and processes that need to be redesigned More specifically, you will be required to :

Help business sectors create, prioritize and adopt AI opportunities, aligned with business priorities
Support business sectors as they develop their AI strategies
Act as the main point of contact for AI between the business sectors and the Office of Desjardins Group’s Chief Data and Analytics Officer
Monitor market trends and internal AI activity across business sectors and support functions to identify opportunities for analytics
Hold brainstorming sessions to explore process-focused AI opportunities in different business sectors to determine which AI projects to prioritize
Create project briefs for AI opportunities, defining the business objective, context, business value, data requirements and complexity
Conduct internal and external monitoring of AI developments and determine their practical implications for the strategy and business sectors
Work with business sectors to lead initiatives to identify AI opportunities across processes, activities and member and client journeys
Prepare clear analyses and recommendations for senior management and decision-making bodies.

What we offer*

Competitive salary and annual bonus
4 weeks of flexible vacation starting in the first year
Defined benefit pension plan that provides predictable, stable income throughout retirement
Group insurance including telemedicine
Reimbursement of health and wellness expenses and telework equipment
Benefits apply based on eligibility criteria.

What You Bring To The Table

Bachelor’s degree in administration, strategy, organizational transformation, technology, analytics or a related field
A minimum of eight years of relevant experience
Please note that other combinations of qualifications and relevant experience may be considered
Significant experience in corporate strategy, transformation or execution of cross-sector initiatives in a large organization
Significant experience structuring complex issues, challenging assumptions and formulating clear, actionable recommendations
Experience in a role that calls for excellent political acumen and the ability to influence individuals with differing priorities, without direct reporting authority
Experience in process analysis or transformation
Knowledge of French is required
Excellent French-language writing, synthesis and communication skills
Advanced knowledge of AI, its business potential, its foundations, its governance principles and the primary risks associated with it; in-depth technical expertise not required
Knowledge of Desjardins or experience in a large financial institution

Action oriented, Customer Focus, Differences, Innovation, Interpersonal Savvy, Nimble learning, Strategic mindset

Equity, Diversity, Inclusion and Accessibility

At Desjardins, we believe in equity, diversity and inclusion. We're committed to welcoming, respecting and valuing people for who they are as individuals, learning from their differences, embracing their uniqueness, and providing a positive workplace for all. At Desjardins, we have zero tolerance for discrimination of any kind. We believe our teams should reflect the diversity of the members, clients and communities we serve.

jobs.description:

To obtain a French translation of the following job posting, please email
careers@ontariohealth.ca
. Requests will be addressed within three business days, and the application window will be extended by three business days.

At Ontario Health, we are committed to developing a strong organizational culture that connects and inspires all team members across the province. Our vision is that together, we will be a leader in health and wellness for all. Our mission is to connect the health system to drive improved and equitable health outcomes, experiences and value. How we work together is reflected through our five values: integrity, inspiration, tenacity, humility and care. 

What Ontario Health offers: 

Role

At Ontario Health, your growth and well-being aren’t just supported—they’re celebrated every step of the way. Here, you have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while shaping a fulfilling and sustainable career. Based on your role, you may receive:

Comprehensive health coverage from day one, with fully paid medical, dental, and vision benefits to support you and your family’s health
Flexible health care or wellness spending accounts, plus an inclusive program to support your overall well-being
A premium defined benefit pension plan, ensuring long-term financial security
Competitive vacation entitlement that encourages time to rest and recharge
Three personal days and two float days annually, providing added flexibility to support work-life balance, in addition to vacation days
Ongoing learning and career development opportunities designed to help you grow, advance, and thrive in your profession
A collaborative, values-driven workplace where integrity, care, humility, inspiration, and tenacity shape everything we do
Opportunities to participate in Communities of Inclusion, fostering belonging, equity, and the sharing of diverse perspectives across our team

Want to make a difference in your career?  Consider this opportunity.

Ontario Health is seeking a strategic, collaborative leader to oversee the multidisciplinary Health System Analytics team of 30–40 professionals. The Director will shape high-impact analytic products, tools, methods and models that inform health system planning, performance measurement, policy, resource allocation and quality improvement.

Combining deep expertise in health care data and analytics with exceptional people leadership, the Director will balance ongoing commitments, strategic initiatives and rapid-response priorities; strengthen organizational capability; and translate complex findings into clear, actionable insights for senior leaders and health system partners.

Here Is What You Will Be Doing

Key Responsibilities

Lead and inspire the team: Provide strategic direction to a multidisciplinary team of 30–40 staff, including managers and individual contributors; foster an open, inclusive and innovative culture; and oversee recruitment, coaching, performance and retention.
Set the analytics agenda: Partner with senior leaders across clinical programs, Regions and corporate portfolios to establish a rolling product plan aligned with organizational priorities.
Deliver trusted analytics: Guide the development of high-quality, methodologically sound, documented and replicable products, including multi-year forecasting and capacity-planning models and analyses of performance, trends and variation.
Advance methods and innovation: Champion leading analytic practices and the responsible adoption of advanced and emerging methods, including artificial intelligence.
Turn evidence into action: Translate complex results into accessible visualizations, presentations, dashboards and concise reports, providing strategic insights and recommendations to senior health system leaders.
Build strong partnerships: Collaborate with internal leaders, clinicians, subject matter experts, researchers, the Ministry of Health and other partners to define needs, manage risks and deliver meaningful outcomes.
Enable sustainable delivery: Oversee work plans, staffing, budgets and financial forecasts, and partner with Digital Excellence in Health on the infrastructure and solutions required to support the team.
Grow analytic capacity: Sponsor the enterprise-wide Analytics Forum, strengthen skills and collaboration, develop external partnerships, and share Ontario Health’s work through stakeholder forums, publications and conferences.
Provide enterprise leadership: Represent Health System Analytics on internal and external committees, governance tables and working groups.

Education And Experience

Here is what you will need to be successful:

Bachelor’s degree in Health or Business Administration, Public Health, Epidemiology, Economics, Data Sciences or another relevant field; a Master’s degree or PhD is an asset.
At least 5 years of relevant work experience, including 3 years experience leading, developing, and supporting teams via projects, programs and/or people leadership preferably within healthcare, public sector, or large complex organizations
Proven ability to manage large, complex data and analytics operations.
Working knowledge of Ontario’s health system and the ability to collaborate effectively with senior leaders, clinicians, researchers, scientists, staff and external partners in a multidisciplinary environment.
Leadership experience in equity, diversity, inclusion and anti-racism is an asset.

Knowledge And Skills

Proven ability to manage high-performing teams to excellent, demonstrable results
Strong judgement, strategic thinking, problem-solving and reasoning skills involving highly complex issues that often have limited precedent.
Broad understanding of the health care and public sector environment, including changing priorities, trends, legislative requirements and/or other internal and external emerging issues and their potential impacts on goals, priorities and activities within the function and across the organization.
Exceptional communication skills, including strong facilitation skills and the ability to create and deliver effective presentations to senior level decision-makers.
Demonstrated relationship-building and stakeholder management skills, including experience leading change initiatives.

Location:
Ontario Health (OH) welcomes applications from candidates across Ontario. Please note that this role follows an in-office work model, requiring employees to work from a designated, approved Ontario Health location.

jobs.title: Vice President, Client Success Strategy & Programs
jobs.description:
Opentext - The Information Company

OpenText is a global leader in information management, where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are the key components of our corporate culture. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to partner with the most highly regarded companies in the world, tackle complex issues, and contribute to projects that shape the future of digital transformation.

AI-First. Future-Driven. Human-Centered.

At OpenText, AI is at the heart of everything we do—powering innovation, transforming work, and empowering digital knowledge workers. We are hiring talent AI can't replace to help us shape the future of information management. Join us.

Role Overview

The Vice President, Client Success Strategy & Programs is a senior leadership role responsible for translating the Client Success Organization (CSO) strategy into an integrated portfolio of priorities, operating plans, and measurable outcomes. Reporting to the Chief Client Officer, this leader brings an enterprise-wide perspective across Professional Services, Renewals, Client Success, and Cloud Operations to strengthen alignment, eliminate duplication, improve execution, and ensure the organization is focused on the opportunities that create the greatest value for clients and the business.

The VP serves as a strategic advisor to the Chief Client Officer and CSO executive team, providing objective analysis, clear recommendations, and disciplined program leadership. The role leads business operations and program management capabilities, establishing the governance, insights, and operating rhythms required to move complex, cross-functional priorities from strategy through execution and measurable outcomes. This leader builds and leads a high-performing team of business operations, project, and program management professionals.

Key Accountabilities

Strategy & Enterprise Planning

Partner with the Chief Client Officer and CSO leadership team to shape and evolve the client success strategy in line with enterprise priorities.
Translate strategy into annual plans, investment priorities, execution roadmaps, and measurable outcomes.
Align goals across Professional Services, Renewals, Client Success, and Cloud Operations, surfacing key dependencies, trade-offs, and risks.
Bring an objective, enterprise-wide lens to planning and executive decision-making.
Guide the organizational, workforce, and capability planning needed to deliver the Client Success strategy.

Executive Partnership & Organizational Alignment

Serve as a trusted advisor to the Chief Client Officer and CSO leaders, bringing strategic perspective, sound judgment, and influence.
Translate complex information into clear executive narratives, recommendations, and decisions.
Connect teams across CSO and partner functions to clarify ownership and drive coordinated execution.
Keep client value and experience at the center of operating and investment decisions.
Represent Client Success priorities in enterprise forums and build alignment with key stakeholders.

Strategic Programs & Transformation

Lead high-impact, cross-functional CSO programs from business case development through execution, adoption, and measurable outcomes.
Ensure initiatives have clear scope, sponsorship, milestones, resources, risks, and success measures.
Provide portfolio visibility that enables timely decisions, issue resolution, and resource alignment.
Lead Client Success planning and execution for mergers, acquisitions, and divestitures, including business readiness and outcome tracking.

Business Management & Performance

Establish an integrated KPI framework that links enterprise goals, functional measures, and accountability.
Lead Client Success performance reporting for the CSO Leadership Team, Executive Leadership Team, and Board.
Use data and insights to identify performance trends, emerging risks, and efficiency opportunities.
Track delivery against strategic, financial, efficiency, and client outcomes.

Experience & Qualifications

15+ years of progressive experience in strategy, business operations, or program leadership within a complex technology organization.
Executive leadership experience, including leading multidisciplinary teams and influencing in a global, matrixed organization.
Proven success translating enterprise strategy into operating plans and measurable results.
Strong financial acumen with experience supporting planning, investment decisions, and business performance.
Strong analytical and program management capabilities, translating complex data into executive insights and disciplined execution.
Experience supporting client-facing functions such as Client Success, Professional Services, Renewals, or Revenue Operations is preferred.
M&A, divestiture, or large-scale integration and separation experience is an asset.
Bachelor’s degree in a related field; an MBA or equivalent advanced degree is considered an asset.

jobs.title: Virtual Chief Information Officer (vCIO)
jobs.description:
Virtual Chief Information Officer (vCIO)

Location: Remote - Canada-wide

Opportunity at Microserve

Position Overview

Microserve is looking for a Virtual Chief Information Officer to provide strategic technology guidance to our core managed services clients. This role leads conversations about how technology roadmaps, investments, and priorities can support each client’s business goals, improve employee productivity, reduce technology friction, and manage risk. This role can be performed remotely from anywhere in Canada.

Bringing broad technology expertise and an understanding of each client’s operating environment and business priorities, this role translates client priorities into practical technology strategies, roadmaps, budgets, and recommendations. Working with client leaders and Microserve teams, the role helps clients make informed technology decisions and prioritize initiatives based on value, risk, readiness, and available budget.

Key Areas Of Accountability

Strategic Technology Leadership

Build a strong understanding of each assigned client’s business strategy, operating model, technology dependence, and growth priorities.
Develop and maintain a multi-year technology roadmap aligned with business objectives, operational requirements, financial capacity.
Translate business needs into clear technology priorities, recommendations, and decision points.
Facilitate strategic technology discussions with client executives and business leaders.

Technology Investment and Budget Planning

Develop and maintain annual and multi-year technology budgets covering lifecycle investments, strategic initiatives, security improvements, and anticipated projects.
Prepare business cases and decision requests that clearly communicate cost, business value, risk, dependencies, and expected outcomes.
Help clients prioritize investments based on business impact, urgency, risk reduction, and available budget.
Monitor roadmap and budget progress and recommend adjustments as client needs change.

Governance, Risk, and Compliance

Provide strategic guidance on technology governance, cybersecurity risk, resilience, privacy, and compliance requirements.
Identify material technology risks and ensure that appropriate recommendations are documented, prioritized, and communicated to client leadership.
Advise clients on the development and maintenance of appropriate IT policies, standards, controls, disaster recovery strategies, and continuity requirements.
Support alignment with relevant cybersecurity frameworks such as CIS Controls, ISO 27001, and NIST, based on each client’s needs and obligations.

Executive Client Engagement

Lead regular strategic technology reviews with client executives and key stakeholders.
Present roadmap progress, investment recommendations, key risks, emerging priorities, and decisions requiring executive sponsorship.
Communicate complex technology topics in clear business language appropriate to the audience.
Build trusted relationships with client leaders and act as a senior point of contact for strategic technology matters.

Solution and Project Governance

Provide business and strategic context during solution development, project scoping, and prioritization.
Confirm that proposed initiatives align with approved roadmaps, business requirements, budgets, security expectations, and intended outcomes.
Collaborate with project managers, architects, security specialists, and service delivery teams during planning and execution.
Participate in project outcome reviews and incorporate lessons learned into future roadmap planning.

Continuous Improvement and Innovation

Identify opportunities to improve employee productivity, service resilience, cybersecurity, technology adoption, and operational efficiency.
Monitor relevant technology and industry developments and assess their potential applicability to client environments.
Collaborate with Microserve teams to improve strategic service offerings, client planning practices, and executive reporting.
Proactively bring forward recommendations supported by practical business cases and implementation considerations.

Pre-Sales Client Engagement

Participate in qualified managed services opportunities with prospective clients to understand their technology priorities, demonstrate Microserve’s strategic technology approach, and begin building the trusted relationship that will continue after onboarding.
Contribute strategic and technical input to proposals for prospective managed services clients and for projects arising from ongoing technology roadmaps, and participate in presenting those proposals to clients.
Support effective transition of new clients from the sales process into onboarding and ongoing strategic technology planning.

Requirements

10+ years of experience in IT management and strategic planning.
3+ years experience in creating and presenting long-term strategic technology roadmaps and budgets
2+ Years of experience with Microsoft 365 Modern Workplace technologies and Microsoft Azure
Demonstrated success in designing and implementing technology solutions and related systems, processes, and controls for a number of rapidly changing organizations
Experience and success in developing and presenting technology business cases, decision requests, and project charters
Demonstrated ability to effectively communicate with individuals at all levels of the organization, including translating technically complex information to varying technical audiences.
Strong general business management and financial acumen
Knowledge of IT infrastructure systems and security operations and a demonstrated ability to resolve complex technology related issues.
Ability to manage and maintain private and confidential information with a high degree of professionalism.
Demonstrated capacity for forming and advancing relationships with both internal and external stakeholders.
Strong resourcefulness, problem solving and project management skills.
Strong written and oral communication skills.
Experienced innovative thinker with proven results in a fast-paced environment.
Intellectual curiosity and passion for technology to stay informed on industry trends.

Desirables

Post-Secondary Certificate or Degree in an IT related field as well as up to date certifications, or equivalent field experience.
Previous IT Management or IT Leadership experience

What do you get?

Highly competitive commission structure designed to reward your success and maximize your earning potential.
Time-off policies that promote work/life balance
Paid time off
Extended Medical and Dental plan from day one
Amazing employee discounts with over 100+ companies (for example: cell phone plans, computer equipment, insurance, groceries, etc.)
Fun Wellness & Engagement Activities – Such as chocolate making, exit rooms, staff holiday parties, to name a few
Community Involvement – We care about giving back to our communities and plan for volunteering events at least once per quarter
Career advancement opportunities
Hybrid working environment for specific roles
Ongoing learning and development opportunities
Professional development & Training reimbursement support

Compensation:
In accordance with the BC Pay Transparency Act the range for this role for BC residents is $100,000-$120,000 annually. Please note the exact salary is determined based on a combination of your relevant experience, skill, competencies, and internal pay equity. If you feel like this role is your dream job and have questions about compensation and benefits, please get in touch with us as we are always happy to discuss further. At Microserve we believe that compensation conversations should always be ongoing.

Microserve is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate based on race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, or other legally protected status. If you would like to request an accommodation, please notify the Recruiter.

Corporate Responsibility

Employee will understand, meet, and live our core values

We Sweep Floors, Openness, Flexibility, Not Stuffy, Customer Driven

About Us

Microserve is an industry leading provider of IT services and solutions to Canadian organizations. Headquartered in Burnaby, BC, with offices in Victoria, Calgary, and Edmonton, we employ over 500 team members, and we’re one of the largest technology solutions providers in Canada. Our 30+ years of continued success and growth stem from our commitment to long term client relationships, adaptability to continuous changes in the IT industry, and our amazing people.

jobs.description:

About Us

The Opportunity

The Director of Planning & Inventory will lead the Ontario Corrugated team’s supply and inventory planning function to ensure customers receive their desired product at the service level they expect. Reporting to the Vice President of Supply Chain & Strategy, this role is critical for building organizational planning capability to support sustainable, profitable growth. It ensures alignment between business strategy and operational execution across production, procurement, and distribution.

The Director of Planning & Inventory leads a team of managers, planners and analysts with a focus on driving structure, establishing best practices for planning tools and processes, and driving continuous improvement initiatives to enhance forecast accuracy, machine utilization, inventory efficiency, and overall supply chain responsiveness.

Direct inventory strategy to balance customer service levels with working capital objectives, minimizing excess/obsolete stock while preventing stockouts

Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing planning team, including senior managers, plant-floor schedulers and inventory analysts

Lead continuous improvement initiatives to enhance planning maturity, process efficiency, and responsiveness to demand volatility
Provide senior leadership with visibility into planning risks, opportunities, and trade-offs to support strategic decision-making

Required

Certificate in Supply Chain Management considered an asset; APICS/ASCM,CPIM, CSCP or CPF

Proven experience in improving capacity/demand planning processes, inventory efficiency, and service levels in a complex, fast-paced environment
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional teams and influence senior stakeholders without direct authority

Excellent analytical skills with an ability to manipulate large data sets and present analyses in a clear, concise manner
Strong communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate data into actionable business insights for various groups of stakeholders
Demonstrated continuous improvement mindset with the ability to identify metrics related to business processes, improving results through effective processes

Opportunities for advancement and internal movement
Education assistance for continuous skill development
Academic scholarships for employees’ children

Retirement savings and wellness initiatives
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Reports to: Chief Executive Officer

Location: Vancouver HQ (hybrid), with operations in Alberta, Ontario and Quebec 

Compensation: $300,000 - $380,000 CAD base + performance bonus + stock options

Who We Are

Fresh Prep is Canada's largest Canadian-owned meal kit company and a certified B Corporation. We deliver chef-created meal kits, prepared meals and a growing grocery marketplace to customers across the country, from production facilities in British Columbia, Alberta, and Quebec, with operations in Ontario. We're a team of over 600 people and over $110M in annual revenue.

Our founders were named EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2025 winners and we've been recognized as one of Deloitte's Best Managed Companies in Canada, one of BC's Top Employers, and one of Globe and Mail's Top Growing Companies.

The Role
You'll own the financial function of a national, multi-province, physical-operations business with subscription economics, which means you need to be fluent in both cohort and contribution margin analysis and in the operating systems required to manage food costs, labour productivity, last mile delivery and freight. 

You'll be accountable for the numbers the Board and our Investors see, capital strategy and the financial rigour that lets the executive team make decisions quickly and correctly.

You'll report to the CEO, sit on the executive team, and be a standing presence in the boardroom. You will also, at points, be the person telling the rest of us that something we want to do doesn't work. We're looking for someone who is comfortable doing that.

What You'll Be DoingFinancial leadership and reporting

Own all financial reporting, including GAAP compliant statements, the annual audit and consolidated reporting across multiple provinces and legal entities.

Own internal management reporting and commentary that gives the executive team and Board timely insight into trends, unit economics, and the drivers behind them: not just what happened, but why.

Own the operating and capital budget process and hold the company to it.

Own the financial metrics framework across the business, including cohort retention, margin, customer payback and facility-level unit economics.

Capital, cash, and financing

Own cash management, working capital, and cash forecasting in a business with meaningful inventory and seasonality.

Manage our lending relationships, credit facilities, and covenant compliance.

Lead financing strategy and execution: debt, asset-based and project finance, equity, and government programs, in partnership with the CEO and founders.

Manage reporting and communication to a capital structure that includes multiple classes of equity and institutional investors, including the obligations that come with it.

Own the government funding agenda, including SR&ED and applicable federal and provincial grant programs.

Transactions and strategic projects

Lead financial diligence, modelling, and integration on acquisitions and other strategic transactions. 

Provide modelling and analytical support for growth decisions: new facilities, capacity investment, category expansion, long-term supply contracts, and technology investment.

Bring financial discipline to pricing and promotional strategy in partnership with the CMO, including the margin envelope within which marketing operates.

Operations partnership

Own cost accounting for a manufacturing and logistics business: standard costs, food cost variance, labour productivity, delivery, freight, and waste.

Partner with Operations on the decisions that determine our gross margin and be a genuine second set of eyes on capital projects.

Support technology and automation decisions with credible business cases and honest post-mortems.

Compliance and governance

Ensure legal and regulatory compliance across all financial functions, including multi-province tax (GST/HST, QST, PST), payroll compliance in four provinces including Quebec, and corporate filings.

Maintain the internal controls appropriate to our scale and to the diligence standards our investors and lenders apply.

Support the Board and its committees with materials, forecasts, and the analysis behind major decisions.

Team

Lead, structure, and develop the finance, accounting and supply chain teams

Continue building systems and processes that create more thinking and less data manipulation. This is a company where the finance team should be spending its time on analysis, not on reconciliation.

What We're Looking For
Required

12+ years in finance and/or accounting, including senior finance leadership in a company at or above $75M in revenue.

CPA designation, with a degree in accounting, finance, or business.

Experience in physical-operations businesses: manufacturing, food production, CPG, or logistics, including hands-on cost accounting ownership.

Demonstrated ownership of an external audit and GAAP reporting.

Experience securing debt financing and managing lender relationships and covenants.

Experience with a modern ERP environment and ancillary tech-stack.

Multi-site operating experience in a manufacturing environment.

Strongly preferred

M&A experience with due diligence, deal structuring and integration integration 

Experience with subscription or recurring-revenue economics alongside physical operations.

Experience with institutional equity investors

Experience preparing a company for a liquidity or capital event.

SR&ED and government grant program experience.

How you work

You reason from data and are honest about what the data doesn't tell you.

You can explain complex financial concepts to a room of operators without either condescending or losing them.

You build environments where other people do their best work, and you develop people rather than accumulating tasks.

You are fluent with AI tooling and actively use it in your own work. Not as a talking point, but because you've found it makes your analysis faster and your team's time better spent. You have a view on where it belongs in a finance function and where it doesn't.

You are willing to be the dissenting voice, and you know how to disagree without being obstructive.

You can toggle between daily finance tasks and strategic board conversations comfortably and can operate with precision in both.

You don’t have an ego, you don’t need to be right and you are happy as long as the decision helps achieve the company’s goals.

What You Can Expect

Competitive executive compensation, performance bonus, and participation in our Employee Stock Option Plan.

Hybrid work, with our HQ in East Vancouver.

Comprehensive executive health benefits including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance.

A Fresh Prep meal plan

A highly impactful seat at the table of a Canadian company that is at the forefront of food innovation 

Fresh Prep is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination of any kind. We value diversity at every level of the company and aim to be representative of the communities we operate in. We endeavour to recruit, develop, and retain the best talent from a diverse candidate pool, and we believe diversity, equity, and inclusion among our team is vital to our success.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and inspire the team: Provide strategic direction to a multidisciplinary team of 30–40 staff, including managers and individual contributors; foster an open, inclusive and innovative culture; and oversee recruitment, coaching, performance and retention.
Set the analytics agenda: Partner with senior leaders across clinical programs, Regions and corporate portfolios to establish a rolling product plan aligned with organizational priorities.

Advance methods and innovation: Champion leading analytic practices and the responsible adoption of advanced and emerging methods, including artificial intelligence.
Turn evidence into action: Translate complex results into accessible visualizations, presentations, dashboards and concise reports, providing strategic insights and recommendations to senior health system leaders.
Build strong partnerships: Collaborate with internal leaders, clinicians, subject matter experts, researchers, the Ministry of Health and other partners to define needs, manage risks and deliver meaningful outcomes.
Enable sustainable delivery: Oversee work plans, staffing, budgets and financial forecasts, and partner with Digital Excellence in Health on the infrastructure and solutions required to support the team.
Grow analytic capacity: Sponsor the enterprise-wide Analytics Forum, strengthen skills and collaboration, develop external partnerships, and share Ontario Health’s work through stakeholder forums, publications and conferences.
Provide enterprise leadership: Represent Health System Analytics on internal and external committees, governance tables and working groups.

Education And Experience

Here is what you will need to be successful:

Bachelor’s degree in Health or Business Administration, Public Health, Epidemiology, Economics, Data Sciences or another relevant field; a Master’s degree or PhD is an asset.
At least 5 years of relevant work experience, including 3 years experience leading, developing, and supporting teams via projects, programs and/or people leadership preferably within healthcare, public sector, or large complex organizations
Proven ability to manage large, complex data and analytics operations.
Working knowledge of Ontario’s health system and the ability to collaborate effectively with senior leaders, clinicians, researchers, scientists, staff and external partners in a multidisciplinary environment.
Leadership experience in equity, diversity, inclusion and anti-racism is an asset.

Knowledge And Skills

Proven ability to manage high-performing teams to excellent, demonstrable results
Strong judgement, strategic thinking, problem-solving and reasoning skills involving highly complex issues that often have limited precedent.
Broad understanding of the health care and public sector environment, including changing priorities, trends, legislative requirements and/or other internal and external emerging issues and their potential impacts on goals, priorities and activities within the function and across the organization.
Exceptional communication skills, including strong facilitation skills and the ability to create and deliver effective presentations to senior level decision-makers.
Demonstrated relationship-building and stakeholder management skills, including experience leading change initiatives.

new_jobs.title: Virtual Chief Information Officer (vCIO)
new_jobs.description:
Virtual Chief Information Officer (vCIO)

Location: Remote - Canada-wide

Opportunity at Microserve

Position Overview

Microserve is looking for a Virtual Chief Information Officer to provide strategic technology guidance to our core managed services clients. This role leads conversations about how technology roadmaps, investments, and priorities can support each client’s business goals, improve employee productivity, reduce technology friction, and manage risk. This role can be performed remotely from anywhere in Canada.

Bringing broad technology expertise and an understanding of each client’s operating environment and business priorities, this role translates client priorities into practical technology strategies, roadmaps, budgets, and recommendations. Working with client leaders and Microserve teams, the role helps clients make informed technology decisions and prioritize initiatives based on value, risk, readiness, and available budget.

Key Areas Of Accountability

Strategic Technology Leadership

Build a strong understanding of each assigned client’s business strategy, operating model, technology dependence, and growth priorities.
Develop and maintain a multi-year technology roadmap aligned with business objectives, operational requirements, financial capacity.
Translate business needs into clear technology priorities, recommendations, and decision points.
Facilitate strategic technology discussions with client executives and business leaders.

Technology Investment and Budget Planning

Develop and maintain annual and multi-year technology budgets covering lifecycle investments, strategic initiatives, security improvements, and anticipated projects.
Prepare business cases and decision requests that clearly communicate cost, business value, risk, dependencies, and expected outcomes.
Help clients prioritize investments based on business impact, urgency, risk reduction, and available budget.
Monitor roadmap and budget progress and recommend adjustments as client needs change.

Governance, Risk, and Compliance

Provide strategic guidance on technology governance, cybersecurity risk, resilience, privacy, and compliance requirements.
Identify material technology risks and ensure that appropriate recommendations are documented, prioritized, and communicated to client leadership.
Advise clients on the development and maintenance of appropriate IT policies, standards, controls, disaster recovery strategies, and continuity requirements.
Support alignment with relevant cybersecurity frameworks such as CIS Controls, ISO 27001, and NIST, based on each client’s needs and obligations.

Executive Client Engagement

Lead regular strategic technology reviews with client executives and key stakeholders.
Present roadmap progress, investment recommendations, key risks, emerging priorities, and decisions requiring executive sponsorship.
Communicate complex technology topics in clear business language appropriate to the audience.
Build trusted relationships with client leaders and act as a senior point of contact for strategic technology matters.

Solution and Project Governance

Provide business and strategic context during solution development, project scoping, and prioritization.
Confirm that proposed initiatives align with approved roadmaps, business requirements, budgets, security expectations, and intended outcomes.
Collaborate with project managers, architects, security specialists, and service delivery teams during planning and execution.
Participate in project outcome reviews and incorporate lessons learned into future roadmap planning.

Continuous Improvement and Innovation

Identify opportunities to improve employee productivity, service resilience, cybersecurity, technology adoption, and operational efficiency.
Monitor relevant technology and industry developments and assess their potential applicability to client environments.
Collaborate with Microserve teams to improve strategic service offerings, client planning practices, and executive reporting.
Proactively bring forward recommendations supported by practical business cases and implementation considerations.

Pre-Sales Client Engagement

Participate in qualified managed services opportunities with prospective clients to understand their technology priorities, demonstrate Microserve’s strategic technology approach, and begin building the trusted relationship that will continue after onboarding.
Contribute strategic and technical input to proposals for prospective managed services clients and for projects arising from ongoing technology roadmaps, and participate in presenting those proposals to clients.
Support effective transition of new clients from the sales process into onboarding and ongoing strategic technology planning.

Requirements

10+ years of experience in IT management and strategic planning.
3+ years experience in creating and presenting long-term strategic technology roadmaps and budgets
2+ Years of experience with Microsoft 365 Modern Workplace technologies and Microsoft Azure
Demonstrated success in designing and implementing technology solutions and related systems, processes, and controls for a number of rapidly changing organizations
Experience and success in developing and presenting technology business cases, decision requests, and project charters
Demonstrated ability to effectively communicate with individuals at all levels of the organization, including translating technically complex information to varying technical audiences.
Strong general business management and financial acumen
Knowledge of IT infrastructure systems and security operations and a demonstrated ability to resolve complex technology related issues.
Ability to manage and maintain private and confidential information with a high degree of professionalism.
Demonstrated capacity for forming and advancing relationships with both internal and external stakeholders.
Strong resourcefulness, problem solving and project management skills.
Strong written and oral communication skills.
Experienced innovative thinker with proven results in a fast-paced environment.
Intellectual curiosity and passion for technology to stay informed on industry trends.

Desirables

Post-Secondary Certificate or Degree in an IT related field as well as up to date certifications, or equivalent field experience.
Previous IT Management or IT Leadership experience

What do you get?

Highly competitive commission structure designed to reward your success and maximize your earning potential.
Time-off policies that promote work/life balance
Paid time off
Extended Medical and Dental plan from day one
Amazing employee discounts with over 100+ companies (for example: cell phone plans, computer equipment, insurance, groceries, etc.)
Fun Wellness & Engagement Activities – Such as chocolate making, exit rooms, staff holiday parties, to name a few
Community Involvement – We care about giving back to our communities and plan for volunteering events at least once per quarter
Career advancement opportunities
Hybrid working environment for specific roles
Ongoing learning and development opportunities
Professional development & Training reimbursement support

Compensation:
In accordance with the BC Pay Transparency Act the range for this role for BC residents is $100,000-$120,000 annually. Please note the exact salary is determined based on a combination of your relevant experience, skill, competencies, and internal pay equity. If you feel like this role is your dream job and have questions about compensation and benefits, please get in touch with us as we are always happy to discuss further. At Microserve we believe that compensation conversations should always be ongoing.

Microserve is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate based on race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, or other legally protected status. If you would like to request an accommodation, please notify the Recruiter.

Corporate Responsibility

Employee will understand, meet, and live our core values

We Sweep Floors, Openness, Flexibility, Not Stuffy, Customer Driven

About Us

Microserve is an industry leading provider of IT services and solutions to Canadian organizations. Headquartered in Burnaby, BC, with offices in Victoria, Calgary, and Edmonton, we employ over 500 team members, and we’re one of the largest technology solutions providers in Canada. Our 30+ years of continued success and growth stem from our commitment to long term client relationships, adaptability to continuous changes in the IT industry, and our amazing people.

new_jobs.title: Vice President, Client Success Strategy & Programs
new_jobs.description:
Opentext - The Information Company

OpenText is a global leader in information management, where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are the key components of our corporate culture. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to partner with the most highly regarded companies in the world, tackle complex issues, and contribute to projects that shape the future of digital transformation.

AI-First. Future-Driven. Human-Centered.

At OpenText, AI is at the heart of everything we do—powering innovation, transforming work, and empowering digital knowledge workers. We are hiring talent AI can't replace to help us shape the future of information management. Join us.

Role Overview

The Vice President, Client Success Strategy & Programs is a senior leadership role responsible for translating the Client Success Organization (CSO) strategy into an integrated portfolio of priorities, operating plans, and measurable outcomes. Reporting to the Chief Client Officer, this leader brings an enterprise-wide perspective across Professional Services, Renewals, Client Success, and Cloud Operations to strengthen alignment, eliminate duplication, improve execution, and ensure the organization is focused on the opportunities that create the greatest value for clients and the business.

The VP serves as a strategic advisor to the Chief Client Officer and CSO executive team, providing objective analysis, clear recommendations, and disciplined program leadership. The role leads business operations and program management capabilities, establishing the governance, insights, and operating rhythms required to move complex, cross-functional priorities from strategy through execution and measurable outcomes. This leader builds and leads a high-performing team of business operations, project, and program management professionals.

Key Accountabilities

Strategy & Enterprise Planning

Partner with the Chief Client Officer and CSO leadership team to shape and evolve the client success strategy in line with enterprise priorities.
Translate strategy into annual plans, investment priorities, execution roadmaps, and measurable outcomes.
Align goals across Professional Services, Renewals, Client Success, and Cloud Operations, surfacing key dependencies, trade-offs, and risks.
Bring an objective, enterprise-wide lens to planning and executive decision-making.
Guide the organizational, workforce, and capability planning needed to deliver the Client Success strategy.

Executive Partnership & Organizational Alignment

Serve as a trusted advisor to the Chief Client Officer and CSO leaders, bringing strategic perspective, sound judgment, and influence.
Translate complex information into clear executive narratives, recommendations, and decisions.
Connect teams across CSO and partner functions to clarify ownership and drive coordinated execution.
Keep client value and experience at the center of operating and investment decisions.
Represent Client Success priorities in enterprise forums and build alignment with key stakeholders.

Strategic Programs & Transformation

Lead high-impact, cross-functional CSO programs from business case development through execution, adoption, and measurable outcomes.
Ensure initiatives have clear scope, sponsorship, milestones, resources, risks, and success measures.
Provide portfolio visibility that enables timely decisions, issue resolution, and resource alignment.
Lead Client Success planning and execution for mergers, acquisitions, and divestitures, including business readiness and outcome tracking.

Business Management & Performance

Establish an integrated KPI framework that links enterprise goals, functional measures, and accountability.
Lead Client Success performance reporting for the CSO Leadership Team, Executive Leadership Team, and Board.
Use data and insights to identify performance trends, emerging risks, and efficiency opportunities.
Track delivery against strategic, financial, efficiency, and client outcomes.

Experience & Qualifications

15+ years of progressive experience in strategy, business operations, or program leadership within a complex technology organization.
Executive leadership experience, including leading multidisciplinary teams and influencing in a global, matrixed organization.
Proven success translating enterprise strategy into operating plans and measurable results.
Strong financial acumen with experience supporting planning, investment decisions, and business performance.
Strong analytical and program management capabilities, translating complex data into executive insights and disciplined execution.
Experience supporting client-facing functions such as Client Success, Professional Services, Renewals, or Revenue Operations is preferred.
M&A, divestiture, or large-scale integration and separation experience is an asset.
Bachelor’s degree in a related field; an MBA or equivalent advanced degree is considered an asset.

OpenText's commitment to diversity and inclusion surpasses legal requirements, evident in our Equal Employment Opportunity Statement of Policy which promotes a respectful and empowering environment for employees of all backgrounds, culture, national origin, race, color, gender, gender identification, sexual orientation, family status, age, veteran status, disability, religion, or other basis protected by applicable laws.

If you need assistance and/or a reasonable accommodation due to a disability during the application or recruiting process, please submit a ticket at Ask HR. Our proactive approach fosters collaboration, innovation, and personal growth, enriching OpenText's vibrant workplace.

AI Usage Disclosure:
As part of our commitment to transparency, we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in various stages of our recruitment process, including resume screening, candidate matching, interview scheduling, and communications. These tools are designed to improve efficiency, reduce bias, and enhance candidate experience. All decisions regarding hiring are made by qualified human professionals, and we continuously monitor our AI systems to ensure fairness and compliance with applicable regulations.
